quests.instruction: The Sun is shining high above the playground, and the slide feels warm. Is it daytime or nighttime?
quests.hint: What is lighting up the sky so brightly?
quests.explanation: When the Sun is up and shining, we have daylight. That is what makes it daytime.
quests.funFact: The Sun is a star. It looks much bigger than the other stars because it is so much closer to us.

quests.instruction: Mia looks out her window and sees the Moon and lots of tiny twinkling stars. When is she looking?
quests.hint: Picture the color of the sky behind those twinkling stars.
quests.explanation: Stars and the Moon are easiest to spot against a dark sky, and the sky is dark at night.
quests.funFact: Stars are far-away suns. They look like tiny dots only because they are very, very far from Earth.

quests.instruction: Which of these do you usually do right after you wake up?
quests.hint: Waking up starts a new day, so pick the thing that starts your day.
quests.explanation: Breakfast is the first meal after a long night of sleep. It gives your body energy for the day.
quests.funFact: Families around the world eat many different breakfasts, like rice, bread, eggs, and porridge.

quests.instruction: Dad turns off the lamp and tucks Lily in with her teddy bear. Is it daytime or nighttime?
quests.hint: Is anyone ready to sleep when the sun is high and bright?
quests.explanation: Tucking in and turning off the lamp means it is time to sleep, and we usually sleep at night.
quests.funFact: Many school-age children need about nine to twelve hours of sleep each night to feel their best.

quests.instruction: The school bus stops, and children walk into their classroom with backpacks on. When is this happening?
quests.hint: Consider the hours when your own school is open.
quests.explanation: Most schools run during the day, when it is light and everyone is awake and ready to learn.
quests.funFact: The first school buses in the United States were pulled by horses!

quests.instruction: Which of these twinkles in the sky when it is dark outside?
quests.hint: One of these needs the Sun to be up. The other does not.
quests.explanation: Stars shine all the time, but we see them best once the sky is dark. Sunshine only comes while the Sun is up.
quests.funFact: The star we call the Sun is the only star close enough to give us daytime.

quests.instruction: The sky slowly turns pink and orange as the Sun peeks over the hills. What is beginning?
quests.hint: Watch which way the light is going: is it arriving or leaving?
quests.explanation: When the Sun peeks over the hills, light is coming back. That is sunrise, the start of a new day.
quests.funFact: Roosters often crow around sunrise, but they can crow at other times of day too.

quests.instruction: Noah splashes in a puddle at the park while the sun warms his face. Which part of the day is it?
quests.hint: Is there enough light to see the whole park clearly?
quests.explanation: Playing outside in warm sunshine is a daytime activity, because the Sun is up and the sky is bright.
quests.funFact: Sunlight helps our bodies make vitamin D, which keeps our bones strong.

quests.instruction: Sofia puts on soft pajamas with little bears on them. When does she most likely do this?
quests.hint: These are the clothes you wear to rest, not to run around.
quests.explanation: Pajamas are comfy clothes for sleeping, so we change into them at night, just before bed.
quests.funFact: Some people say pajamas first became popular in England after traveling there from India.

quests.instruction: A grown-up reads a picture book aloud while the bedroom lights are turned low. When is it?
quests.hint: Dim lights and a quiet voice go with getting ready for what?
quests.explanation: Bedtime stories help children relax and get sleepy, so they are read at night before sleep.
quests.funFact: Reading to children for even a few minutes a day helps them learn new words.

quests.instruction: Zara opens her lunch box in the busy school cafeteria. Is this daytime or nighttime?
quests.hint: Lunch sits in the middle of the school day.
quests.explanation: Lunch is eaten in the middle of the day, when schools are open and the Sun is up.
quests.funFact: The word lunch is a short form of an older English word, luncheon.

quests.instruction: Which picture would you draw to show the night sky?
options: A blue sky with a bright Sun
quests.hint: Colors matter here: what color is the sky when the Sun is out of view?
quests.explanation: At night our part of Earth is turned away from the Sun, so the sky looks dark and stars can show.
quests.funFact: Artists often mix black with deep blue to paint a night sky that glows.

quests.instruction: Sunshine spills across Leo's bed and his alarm goes off. What is Leo about to do?
quests.hint: Alarm clocks ring to help people begin something.
quests.explanation: An alarm and morning light tell Leo that a new day has started, so he gets up.
quests.funFact: Early alarm clocks used bells and were first built hundreds of years ago.

quests.instruction: It is so dark outside that Dan needs a flashlight to see the garden path. When is this happening?
quests.hint: You would not usually need a flashlight on a bright sunny path.
quests.explanation: A flashlight helps us see when the Sun is not lighting the sky. That is how nighttime feels outdoors.
quests.funFact: Many flashlights now use tiny LED lights that stay bright for hours.

quests.instruction: Birds chirp in the trees while children ride bikes in the bright sun. Which time of day is it?
quests.hint: Who needs lots of light to ride safely?
quests.explanation: Bike riding and birdsong fit a bright day, when people and many birds are up and about.
quests.funFact: Bicycles were invented almost 200 years ago, and the first ones had no pedals.

quests.instruction: Which light helps us see when the sky is dark?
quests.hint: One of these is switched on by hand.
quests.explanation: When the Sun is not lighting our sky, we use lamps and other lights to see indoors.
quests.funFact: The first electric light bulbs that people could use at home were made in the late 1800s.

quests.instruction: Kids line up outside for recess and put on their sun hats. When is recess happening?
quests.hint: Hats like these protect people from something that is up in the sky.
quests.explanation: Sun hats shade our faces from the Sun, so we wear them when the Sun is up and shining.
quests.funFact: Wearing a hat with a brim helps shade your eyes and face from the Sun.

quests.instruction: Max brushes his teeth and says, "Good night, Mom!" What time is it?
quests.hint: Consider what people say just before they fall asleep.
quests.explanation: Saying good night and brushing teeth are part of the bedtime routine, which happens at night.
quests.funFact: Brushing for two minutes helps clean away sticky plaque from your teeth.

quests.instruction: A rooster crows, the sky glows with light, and the smell of toast drifts down the hall. Which part of the day is just beginning?
quests.hint: Toast and a bright sky both point to a fresh start.
quests.explanation: Morning begins when the sky brightens. It is the time when many people eat toast and start their day.
quests.funFact: Sunrise happens a little earlier or later each day, depending on the season.

quests.instruction: Crickets chirp softly in the yard while the whole family sleeps. When is this?
quests.hint: Ask yourself when the house is quiet and the lights are off.
quests.explanation: Crickets often sing in the evening and night, and a sleeping family means it is dark and late.
quests.funFact: Only male crickets chirp, and they make the sound by rubbing their wings together.

quests.instruction: A farmer picks juicy apples in the orchard under the warm sun. What part of the day is it?
quests.hint: Picking fruit is easier when you can see the branches clearly.
quests.explanation: Farmers work in the orchard in daylight, when they can see the ripe fruit and the sun keeps them warm.
quests.funFact: An apple tree can take several years to grow before it makes its first apples.

quests.instruction: Which of these usually happens at bedtime?
quests.hint: Recess is a school event. Bedtime is something else.
quests.explanation: At bedtime we turn off the lights so our rooms are dark and it is easier to fall asleep.
quests.funFact: Darkness tells our bodies it is time to rest by helping us feel sleepy.

quests.instruction: Which of these goes with a sunny day?
quests.hint: One of these helps you see in the dark. The other helps with bright light.
quests.explanation: Sunglasses make bright sunlight easier on our eyes, so they go with sunny, daytime weather.
quests.funFact: Sunglasses became popular because they protect eyes from the bright light of the Sun.

quests.instruction: A teacher greets her class: "Good morning, everyone!" Is it daytime or nighttime?
quests.hint: Morning belongs to the part of the day when we have sunlight.
quests.explanation: Morning is the first part of the day, so it is part of daytime.
quests.funFact: Daytime includes the morning, the afternoon, and the early evening.

quests.instruction: After the stars come out and the street goes quiet, what are most families doing?
quests.hint: Most schools are closed when the sky is full of stars.
quests.explanation: At night, most people are resting, because bodies need sleep to grow, heal, and think clearly.
quests.funFact: Sleeping helps your body repair itself and helps your brain store what you learned.

quests.instruction: Two friends build a sandcastle at the beach while the sun glitters on the waves. When is this?
quests.hint: Could they see their castle well if the sky was dark?
quests.explanation: Building sandcastles is easier in daylight, when you can see the sand, the waves, and your tools.
quests.funFact: Sand is made of tiny broken pieces of rock and shells.

quests.instruction: What would you say to a friend just before you both fall asleep?
quests.hint: Decide what these words mean about the time you are saying them.
quests.explanation: Good night is a farewell for the end of the day. Good morning is a hello for when a day begins.
quests.funFact: People say good night in every language, with words like buenas noches and bonne nuit.

quests.instruction: Which one does NOT belong with daytime?
quests.correctAnswer: Stars twinkling in a dark sky
options: Stars twinkling in a dark sky
quests.hint: Most of the stars are hard to see in bright sunshine.
quests.explanation: Stars are hard to see in the daytime because sunlight fills the sky with so much light.
quests.funFact: Stars do not go away in the day. Sunlight is so bright that it hides them.

quests.instruction: Which of these does not go with a nighttime scene?
quests.hint: Something here needs the Sun to be up.
quests.explanation: Bright sunshine happens in daytime. Pajamas and quiet rest fit nighttime.
quests.funFact: Our part of Earth gets no direct sunshine at night because it is turned away from the Sun.

quests.instruction: After the long night, the sky gets bright again. What lights up the sky?
quests.hint: Consider what is big enough to light the whole sky.
quests.explanation: The Sun rises after the night and fills the whole sky with light. Streetlamps only light a small area.
quests.funFact: Every morning the Sun appears to rise, but really our Earth is turning toward it.
